facts.text: Pablo Pena is situated in Starr County, Texas, near the Rio Grande river which forms the international border with Mexico.
The region around Pablo Pena was initially colonized under Spanish and Mexican rule through land grants issued between 1749 and 1846.
Early ranching in Pablo Pena revolved around cattle and sheep herding on narrow strips of land called porciones along the river.
The arrival of the railroad in 1925 provided modest connectivity to the sparsely populated area of Pablo Pena.
Pablo Pena experiences a hot semi-arid climate with summer highs often reaching 98 degrees Fahrenheit during July and August.
Proximity to the Falcon International Reservoir supports irrigation for vegetable and crop production in the Pablo Pena agribusiness economy.
